Class EnumerationAdapterTest

java.lang.Object
myTest.EnumerationAdapterTest
public class EnumerationAdapterTest extends Object
Test suite for the EnumerationAdapter class.

This test suite verifies the functionality of the EnumerationAdapter class, which implements the HEnumeration interface to iterate over elements of a VectorAdapter or SubListAdapter. The tests cover various scenarios including normal iteration, edge cases, and error conditions.

Test Case Design

The test cases are designed to validate the behavior of EnumerationAdapter against the specifications of Java 1.4.2 Enumeration interface. The test design includes categories for basic functionality, edge cases, error conditions, and sublist-specific behavior.

Testing Framework Information

This test suite utilizes JUnit 4.13 testing framework with Hamcrest 1.3 matchers for assertions. These dependencies are located as follows:

  • JUnit 4.13: JUnit/junit-4.13.jar
  • Hamcrest Core 1.3: JUnit/hamcrest-core-1.3.jar

    • testHasMoreElementsAtTheBeginning

      public void testHasMoreElementsAtTheBeginning()
      Test method to verify the behavior of hasMoreElements() at the beginning of enumeration.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that hasMoreElements() returns true when the enumeration is at the beginning of a non-empty collection, indicating that there are elements available for iteration.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate the initial state of the enumeration. After setup, the enumeration should be positioned at the start of the collection and should report that more elements are available.

      Test Description:

      The test immediately checks if hasMoreElements() returns true, since the enumeration hasn't started iterating yet.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HEnumeration is created from vector.elements()

      - Enumeration is at the starting position (cursor = 0)

      Post-Condition:

      - Enumeration state remains unchanged

      - No elements have been consumed by the enumeration

      Expected Results:

      hasMoreElements() should return true, indicating there are elements available for iteration.

    • testHasMoreElementsInTheMiddle

      public void testHasMoreElementsInTheMiddle()
      Test method to verify the behavior of hasMoreElements() during middle of enumeration.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that hasMoreElements() returns true when the enumeration is in the middle of iterating through a collection, indicating that there are still more elements available.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate the intermediate state of the enumeration. After consuming some elements, the enumeration should still report that more elements are available if the end hasn't been reached.

      Test Description:

      The test creates an enumeration and consumes the first two elements. It then checks if hasMoreElements() returns true, indicating that there are still elements remaining for iteration.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HEnumeration is created from vector.elements()

      - Two elements have been consumed using nextElement()

      Post-Condition:

      - Enumeration cursor has advanced to position 2

      - Two elements have been consumed

      Expected Results:

      hasMoreElements() should return true, indicating there are still elements available for iteration.

    • testHasMoreElementsAtTheEnd

      public void testHasMoreElementsAtTheEnd()
      Test method to verify the behavior of hasMoreElements() at the end of enumeration.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that hasMoreElements() returns false when all elements in the collection have been consumed, indicating that no more elements are available for iteration.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate the terminal state of the enumeration, after consuming all elements, since no more elements are available.

      Test Description:

      The test creates an enumeration and iterates through all elements until hasMoreElements() returns false. It then verifies that hasMoreElements() consistently returns false after all elements have been consumed.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HEnumeration is created from vector.elements()

      - All elements have been consumed using nextElement()

      Post-Condition:

      - Enumeration cursor is at the end position (cursor = 5)

      - All elements have been consumed

      Expected Results:

      hasMoreElements() should return false, indicating no more elements are available for iteration.

    • testNextElementProperIteration

      public void testNextElementProperIteration()
      Test method to verify proper iteration sequence using nextElement().

      Summary:

      This test verifies that nextElement() returns elements in the correct order throughout the whole iteration.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate the complete iteration sequence and verify proper exhaustion of the enumeration.

      Test Description:

      The test iterates through all elements of the enumeration, verifying each element matches the expected value. Finally, it verifies that hasMoreElements() returns false after all elements have been consumed.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HEnumeration is created from vector.elements()

      - Enumeration is at the starting position

      Post-Condition:

      - Enumeration cursor is at the end position (cursor = 5)

      - All elements have been consumed

      Expected Results:

      Elements should be returned in sequence: "1", "2", "3", null, "5"

      hasMoreElements() should return false after the fifth element is consumed

    • testNextElementThrowsException

      public void testNextElementThrowsException()
      Test method to verify that nextElement() throws NoSuchElementException when exhausted.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that nextElement() throws NoSuchElementException when called after complete consumption, ensuring proper exception handling.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate the exception handling behavior of the enumeration when it's exhausted.

      Test Description:

      The test first iterates through all elements until hasMoreElements() returns false. Then attempts to call nextElement() again and expects a NoSuchElementException to be thrown.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - HEnumeration is created from vector.elements()

      - All elements have been consumed using nextElement()

      - hasMoreElements() returns false

      Post-Condition:

      - Enumeration remains in exhausted state

      - NoSuchElementException is thrown

      Expected Results:

      nextElement() should throw NoSuchElementException when called on an exhausted enumeration.

    • testNextElementDuplicates

      public void testNextElementDuplicates()
      Test method to verify proper iteration with duplicate elements using nextElement().

      Summary:

      This test verifies that nextElement() correctly handles collections containing duplicate elements.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate enumeration behavior with duplicate values, to ensure no other operation is performed.

      Test Description:

      The test creates a VectorAdapter with three string of "0". It then iterates through the enumeration, verifying that each call to nextElement() returns the same value.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 3 identical elements: ["0", "0", "0"]

      - HEnumeration is created from vector.elements()

      - Enumeration is at the starting position

      Post-Condition:

      - Enumeration cursor is at the end position

      - All three elements have been consumed

      Expected Results:

      All three calls to nextElement() should return "0"

      hasMoreElements() should return false after the third element is consumed

    • testNestedSubListNextElementProperIteration

      public void testNestedSubListNextElementProperIteration()
      Test method to verify proper iteration sequence using nextElement() on a nested sublist.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that nextElement() returns elements in the correct order from a nested sublist (sublist of a sublist).

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate the complete iteration sequence of a nested sublist enumeration. This ensures that sublist operations work correctly even with multiple nested levels.

      Test Description:

      The test creates a multiple sublist from the main vector. It then iterates through the nested sublist enumeration, verifying each element matches the expected value.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - First SubListAdapter is created from indices 1 to 5 of the main vector

      - Second SubListAdapter is created from indices 1 to 3 of the first sublist

      - HEnumeration is created from the nested sublist.elements()

      - Enumeration is at the starting position

      Post-Condition:

      - Enumeration cursor is at the end position

      - Both elements of the nested sublist have been consumed

      Expected Results:

      Elements should be returned in sequence: "3", null

      hasMoreElements() should return false after the second element is consumed
